To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transport of model drugs from emulsified systems is influenced by the presence of nonionic surfactants, and the effect is dependent on the nature of the drug and the surfactant.
the addition of excess surfactants to emulsions increases the drug solubilization capacity and reduces the diffusion coefficients of model drugs in emulsions.

(1) the presence of excess surfactants in emulsions can have significant effects on the transport kinetics of drugs; (2) these effects are related to the physicochemical properties of the drug and the excess surfactant and (3) the transport kinetics can be controlled by adjusting the surfactant concentration and/or by using a combination of two or more surfactants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transport of small molecules in emulsions.
the influence of the surfactant on the transport of the model drugs through the emulsions and the influence of the model drug on the emulsion structure and transport kinetics.
the transport of drugs in emulsions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in emulsion formulations containing a nonionic surfactants as emulsifier, the excess surfactant can affect the transport kinetics of model drugs in the system.
the presence of excess emulsifier has a significant influence on the transport kinetics of PAA, benzocaine and phenol in emulsions.
the presence of excess surfactants in emulsions does not affect the transport rate constants of model drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transport of drugs through the emulsion system is influenced by the presence of excess surfactants.
the addition of excess surfactants to emulsion systems can be used to control the release rate of a drug from emulsion systems.
the addition of excess surfactants to an emulsion system can have a dramatic effect on the rate of drug transport.
